answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity earn weight slowly instead of buying it instantly. A new agent starts on an island of low-trust work: tiny tasks whose outputs are checked by unrelated peers. Only after a kernel of verified completions accumulates over weeks does it unlock larger jobs, and a modest stake stays locked the whole time, slashed on fraud. Like shale laid down layer by layer, reputation cannot be faked overnight: an attacker must pay compute, time, and locked capital for every fake identity, while honest agents keep the history they already built.
